html:
SMTO-GML-0027 — Google didn't allow SMTO to do this in your Gmail

GUID: a0d0743b-45ca-4959-96f3-bac677f044c6
Slug: gmail-scope-required
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO tried to do something in your Gmail that Google hasn't allowed for this connection. You may not have granted that permission when you signed in, or your Google account's rules block it. The step didn't run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In a conversation, ask SMTO to connect your Gmail account again and open the Google link it gives you. A new sign-in lets you grant the permission that is missing.
  2. On the Google page, tick every permission box shown, then select Allow. If a box is left unticked, SMTO can't do the actions that need it, such as managing filters or deleting emails forever.
  3. If Google still refuses, or this is a work or school account, select Copy error details and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Your organization's Google settings or SMTO's Google app settings may block this action, and only an administrator can change them.

What success looks like

  • SMTO completes the Gmail action, for example the filter is created or the emails are removed.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages SMTO; they may need to add the missing permission to SMTO's Gmail OAuth App entry. Never paste your Google password or sign-in codes into a conversation.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail access was refused: either the saved Gmail account lacks a required scope (gmail.settings.basic for filters, https://mail.google.com/ for permanent deletion), or the Gmail API returned HTTP 403 for this account or resource.

What this means

  • Legacy filter validation proves a required settings scope is absent, while the generic mailbox wrapper also maps provider access denial to this scope-related compatibility kind. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Legacy filter validation proves a required settings scope is absent, while the generic mailbox wrapper also maps provider access denial to this scope-related compatibility kind.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare explicit granted-scope evidence with the safe provider denial reason before requesting broader consent.

How to fix it

  • GmailService._filters and _permanent_delete raise gmail_scope_required with missing_scope when granted_scopes lacks the required scope; GmailService._call maps any provider 403 to the same code. If missing_scope is present, add it to the Gmail OAuth App parameter's scopes if absent and reconnect the account via gmail.connect; otherwise read the 403 reason in the Server log (Workspace policy, disabled API, resource permission) and resolve it with the account's Google administrator.
  • Request the specific scope only when it is known missing; otherwise inspect and resolve the provider's account/resource access denial.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual missing scope or authorization policy is resolved for the intended account.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
